newsitem.title: UK: Argentina to tap Japanese market before end-year.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to tap Japanese market before end-year.

text.p: Argentina wants to raise about $300 million on the Japanese market, effectively completing all its borrowing needs for the year, Economy Minister Rique Fernandez said in an interview on Tuesday.

Fernandez, who is leading the largest Argentine economic mission to Britain since the 1982 Falklands War, also said that the country planned to raise some $8.5 billion on the international markets next year, unchanged from 1996.

"We have almost completed (our borrowing for 1996). There is an operation in the order of $300 million that may be done before the end of 1996...(which) we may be doing in the samurai bonds, the Japanese market. We are in the process of deciding," he told Reuters.
Borrowing on the domestic market is also almost complete.
"If there are some operations they will be very minor ones."
Next year's financial programme, including a fiscal deficit of $3 billion and debt amoritsation of $8.7 billion, will total $14.1 billion.

Apart from tapping the international markets, $3.2 billion will come from the domestic market, $1.3 billion from international financial institutions and the rest from privatisation and other capital revenue, he said.
